instructions.question: Is every requirement stated in `task` shown as implemented by the checks that ran (`checks`, and `check_results` when that field is present) and by the files that were edited (`edits`, and `edit_stats` when that field is present)?
instructions.note: Go through the requirements stated in `task` one at a time and ask what in the checks and the edited files would show it was met: edge cases, ordering, boundaries, defaults and error handling count. A statement in `final_message` that the work is done is not evidence. When `task` only points to a file for its requirements, judge what that pointer and the evidence allow.

criteria.true: Every stated requirement is covered by evidence from the checks and the edited files.
criteria.false: At least one stated requirement has no such evidence, or the evidence points at a failure.

instructions.question: Is there a requirement stated in `task` that the checks that ran (`checks`, and `check_results` when that field is present) and the files that were edited (`edits`, and `edit_stats` when that field is present) do not show as implemented?
instructions.note: Go through the requirements stated in `task` one at a time and ask what in the checks and the edited files would show it was met: edge cases, ordering, boundaries, defaults and error handling count. A statement in `final_message` that the work is done is not evidence. When `task` only points to a file for its requirements, judge what that pointer and the evidence allow.

criteria.true: At least one stated requirement has no evidence of being implemented, or the evidence points at a failure.
criteria.false: Every stated requirement is covered by evidence from the checks and the edited files.

instructions.question: Does the evidence leave a requirement stated in `task` unverified: one that no check in `checks` (or `check_results`, when present) exercises, or that `final_message` itself says was not checked?
instructions.note: Go through the requirements stated in `task` one at a time. A requirement counts as verified only when a check that ran and passed would have failed had it been missed. Edited files (`edits`, and `edit_stats` when present) show what was touched, not that it was verified.

criteria.true: At least one stated requirement is not exercised by any check that ran, or the message says it was not checked.
criteria.false: Every stated requirement is exercised by a check that ran and passed.

instructions.question: Is it likely that the work leaves a requirement stated in `task` unmet in a case that a quick check would not reveal: an edge case, an ordering or tie-break rule, a boundary, a default that differs from the obvious one, or error handling?
instructions.note: Read the requirements in `task` for clauses that are easy to overlook, then use the checks (`checks`, and `check_results` when present) and the edited files (`edits`, and `edit_stats` when present) to see whether the work looks thorough enough to have handled them. A statement in `final_message` that the work is done is not evidence.

criteria.true: It is likely that at least one such requirement is unmet.
criteria.false: It is unlikely that any stated requirement is unmet.
